named_subject: a giraffe's head and upper neck, seen in close-up with two ossicones, an eye mark and a long muzzle
action: The giraffe head holds roughly still while it tilts from pointing up-right to level, shrinks for a few frames, then grows larger again, with little change at the mouth.
identity_gap: The head uses the doodle's own parts (the flag-shaped and P-shaped ossicones, the arrow eye, the cheek loop and the muzzle line), but most of the doodle's long neck with its extra strokes is cropped out of frame.
notes: The film shows the giraffe chewing with its mouth opening and closing and the head turning slightly, while the animation instead changes the head's size and tilt in steps (frame 5 tilt change, frame 9 shrink, frame 12 enlarge) and the ossicones do not move with the head. The change that would help most is to keep the head at one scale and drive the muzzle and jaw lines to open and close in time with the chewing in the film.
